steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An exoplanet is a planet orbiting a star other than the Sun; over 5,500 have been confirmed

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The transit method detects exoplanets by measuring the dip in a star's brightness as a planet passes in front

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The radial velocity (Doppler) method detects the wobble of a star caused by an orbiting planet

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The habitable zone (Goldilocks zone) is the region around a star where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How does the transit method detect exoplanets? | Q: What is the habitable zone? | Q: Name two methods of detecting exoplanets.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: By monitoring a star's brightness over time — a periodic dip indicates a planet passing in front (transiting), blocking a fraction of the star's light. | The region around a star where temperatures allow liquid water on a planet's surface — not too hot and not too cold ('Goldilocks zone'). | Transit method (dip in brightness) and radial velocity/Doppler method (wobble in star's spectrum).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Transit method = brightness dip; radial velocity = spectrum wobble — know both The habitable zone depends on the star's luminosity — hotter stars have wider, more distant HZs Over 5,500 exoplanets confirmed (as of 2024) — use this number The Drake equation is speculative but shows what factors affect the likelihood of life
